summary.headline: BirlaNu Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.6% to Rs 1,174 crores and EBITDA 35% to Rs 80 crores, with Parador still loss-making at Rs 13 crores.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew 10% to Rs 824 crores and EBITDA rose nearly 70% to Rs 97 crores, with margins up over 420 bps, led by Roofs and Pipes. Pipes revenue fell 11% and volumes fell 27% on a sharp PVC resin price swing, yet EBITDA margin expanded 660 bps on mix and pricing. Parador swung to a Rs 13 crore EBITDA loss, which management attributed mostly to timing items expected to normalise in H2. Gross borrowings fell about Rs 100 crores to Rs 758 crores and working capital was cut by about Rs 100 crores year-on-year.

financial_highlights.change: nearly +70% YoY; margin up over 420 bps
vs profit of Rs 5 crores last year
down from Rs 852 crores at March 2026

segments.name: Roofs
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 517 crores, up 17% (volume growth about 10%), a record quarter with market share up about 100 bps and EBITDA margin 18.2%.

segments.name: Walls (boards, panels, blocks)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 14% with margin 10.2%, up 270 bps; management says the current portfolio can reach 12-14%.

segments.name: Pipes
segments.commentary: Revenue down 11% and volumes down 27% after PVC resin prices rose about 60% in March then fell about 30% in April; EBITDA margin still up over 660 bps on mix and pricing.

segments.name: Construction Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 11% despite raw material prices rising over 50%; tile and project slowdowns hit demand temporarily.

segments.name: Parador (Europe)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat YoY in euro terms; order book up over 10%; EBITDA loss of Rs 13 crores includes about EUR 1 million of one-time SAP and front-loaded maintenance costs.

segments.name: Clean Coats
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 9 crores in Q1; now reported under Pipes and Construction Chemicals on a consolidated basis.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give numeric FY27 targets but said it hopes to keep beating internal targets, which it has done for the last two quarters.
Pipes: expects moderate growth in seasonally weak Q2, with PVC prices stabilising on government measures.
Parador: expects H2 recovery and says it is looking at more than breaking even this year; BCG cost programme targeted at 300-400 bps EBITDA margin uplift, with full impact around Q4.
Boards: Andhra Pradesh (Nellore) plant to be commissioned by Q4 FY27; new Telangana board plant expected to add Rs 300-350 crores revenue and Rs 75-85 crores EBITDA once ramped up.
Borrowings expected to stay elevated near term, reducing progressively as Nellore board plant starts contributing from late FY27.
Management cites a longer-term aim of doubling the business, about Rs 8,000-9,000 crores revenue over 2-3 years; about Rs 500 crores capex is allocated to named projects.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad (Telangana) greenfield designer board plant approved; capex about Rs 167 crores including land (about Rs 145-150 crores excluding land), asset turn 0.9x, target revenue Rs 140 crores.
Nellore boards and panels plant: Rs 127 crores capex, civil work under way, machinery installation to start from next month; around 90-100% of orders placed.
OPVC capex of Rs 40 crores completed in July 2026.
Boards capacity at 80-90% utilisation, described as capacity constrained.
Solar capacity commissioned at 2 manufacturing facilities.
demand_pricing: Roofs growth driven by rural demand, price support and elevated steel sheet prices pushing demand toward fibre cement; management characterised the quarter as secondary sales.
Board industry is about Rs 1,500-2,000 crores, growing 10-14% a year; 5-7 organised players and 15-20% imports; industry margins in the high teens.
Pipes: sharp April demand drop after resin price moves; management says Q2 indications are positive but PVC pipe market remains volatile.
Parador: commercial and new-market revenue each under 5% today; line of sight to adding Rs 20-30 million (EUR) revenue over the next couple of years, lifting their combined share to about 20%.
Construction Chemicals: raw material inflation above 50% and tile-industry disruption from the Middle East conflict.
Working capital: receivables down close to 30% after tighter credit controls; fibre inventory substantially reduced over 6-8 months.

qa_highlights.question: What covenant breaches were waived by banks and what is the borrowing plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Breaches were on debt-equity covenants; borrowings were Rs 852 crores at March 2026 and Rs 758 crores at June 2026, and they will stay elevated near term until Nellore starts contributing from late FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How does Parador grow over the next 2-3 years and what is the cost upside?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees at least Rs 20-30 million of added revenue from US, India, UK and Middle East commercial channels, DIY expansion in Europe, and Italy and Eastern Europe orders; BCG cost programme targets at least 300-400 bps EBITDA uplift.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Boards market and why is BirlaNu's margin below the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Market is Rs 1,500-2,000 crores growing 10-14%; the company's wall segment blended margin is 10-11% while new standalone board plants target 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Roofs margins and growth one-offs or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-offs or inventory gains; growth was about 10% volume plus price, and the mix is primarily secondary sales in the season.

qa_highlights.question: Is Parador manufacturing moving to India, and is a rights issue planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Options including India are being evaluated for cost-to-serve and supply-chain diversification, subject to quality; the CFO said debt-equity is 0.68x and the Board decides on any rights issue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Telangana plant's economics and the Nellore capex status?
qa_highlights.answer: Telangana asset turn is 0.9x on about Rs 145-150 crores investment excluding land; Nellore is in civil construction with about 90-100% of orders placed.

risks_watch: Pipes: PVC resin prices swung about +60% in March and about -30% in April; Q2 is seasonally weak and management expects only moderate growth, with price stabilisation dependent on government measures and the market still volatile.

Parador: Rs 13 crore EBITDA loss in Q1; recovery to more than breakeven this year depends on H2 order conversion, the BCG cost programme (300-400 bps uplift, full impact around Q4) and the Rs 20-30 million revenue line of sight.

Leverage and covenants: debt-equity covenant breaches were waived by banks; gross borrowings Rs 758 crores at June 2026 and expected to stay elevated until Nellore boards plant contributes from late FY27. Board to decide on any rights issue.

Execution: Nellore boards plant (Rs 127 crores capex) targeted for Q4 FY27 commissioning; Hyderabad plant (about Rs 167 crores including land) approved and timeline not yet given; boards capacity at 80-90% utilisation.

Sustainability of Roofs and working capital gains: Roofs growth was largely secondary sales in a season with elevated steel prices and strong rural demand; receivables cut about 30% and fibre inventory reduced over 6-8 months.
Raw material, freight, currency and labour cost inflation; Construction Chemicals raw material prices up over 50% amid Middle East conflict and tile-industry disruption.
key_quotes: So any target I share with you is a hazardous one.
We are looking at growth overall from a rev enue perspective, and we are looking at more than breaking even this year.

But I think the positive trajectory of the financial performance is also an indicator that there is some volume uplift we are getting because of those rebranding decisions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the India business, Roofs, Walls and the H2 outlook, but cautious on Pipes volatility and Parador, which management says is a near-term turbulence. Management declined to give numeric FY27 targets, saying "any target I share with you is a hazardous one", and deferred on rights issue and capital structure to the Board.
